findings.title: Every Imaging-screen capture loses its filter: FITS has no FILTER card, filename says "NoFilter", DB filter column is empty
findings.what_happened: With the simulated filter wheel connected and reporting slot 2 = R, I took a 30 s light. The file was written as /tmp/Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_0001.fits, its header contains no FILTER keyword at all, and captured_images.filter is the empty string. findings.expected: FILTER = 'Ha' in the FITS header, 'Ha' in the filename, and 'Ha' in captured_images.filter - the wheel is connected and the app already knows and displays the active filter name on the same screen.
findings.repro: 1. Onboard with the Sim backend (camera + filter wheel with L R G B Ha OIII SII). 2. Equipment -> Connect All. 3. Imaging -> Capture tab, exposure 30 -> Snapshot. 4. Click the Ha chip in the bottom banner, Snapshot again. 5. `python3` dump of the FITS header and `sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select file_name,filter from captured_images'`.

findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/imaging_bottom_banner.dart:552 (FilterWheelSelector built with no onFilterSelected); packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/filter_wheel_selector.dart:32,88-91 (callback declared, never supplied); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/imaging_service/persistence.dart:57

findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently in my own instance (display :87, profile imaging-guiding-verify). The sim filter wheel was connected with names [L,R,G,B,Ha,OIII,SII] and the log shows `api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=4` at 15:22:48; the 5 s light taken at 15:23:08 was written as /tmp/ns-verify-caps/Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_0002.fits with NO FILTER card (verified by dumping the 80-char header cards), and `sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select file_name,filter from captured_images'` returns filter='' for all 22 frames in the profile. Code confirms: imaging_bottom_banner.dart:552 is the only construction of FilterWheelSelector and it omits onFilterSelected (declared filter_wheel_selector.dart:24/32, fired at :88-91); camera_panel.dart and capture_panel.dart contain no filter control at all, so the banner strip is the Imaging screen's only filter UI; persistence.dart:55 reads `filter: exposureSettings.filter`. Two corrections. (1) 'grep shows ZERO callers anywhere pass it / nothing ever writes the filter name into exposureSettingsProvider' is overstated: dashboard/widgets/capture_settings_card.dart:411,439 and widgets/capture_settings_panel.dart:420,439 both do `copyWith(filter: ...)` after the wheel settles — the Dashboard capture card tags frames correctly (capture_settings_panel.dart has no call sites, it is dead code). (2) The sequencer path is unaffected: FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context (api/imaging.rs:3384) sets filter from ctx.filter_name and save_fits_file_rich writes FILTER + FILTPOS at :3692-3696. findings.title: FITS DATE-OBS records the END of the exposure, not the start - off by exactly EXPTIME
findings.what_happened: 30 s exposure: native log 'Starting 30s exposure' at 14:04:37.85, 'Exposure complete' at 14:05:09.05; the FITS says DATE-OBS = '2026-08-01T14:05:09.000Z'. 5 s exposure: start 14:07:56.16, complete 14:08:01.93, DATE-OBS = '2026-08-01T14:08:01.000Z'. In both cases DATE-OBS equals the completion timestamp, i.e. it is late by exactly the exposure duration. The Dart side takes `capturedImage.timestamp` (the download/completion time returned by the bridge) and hands it straight to FitsWriteHeader.captureTimestamp, even though the same function already holds `exposureStartedAt`.
findings.expected: DATE-OBS is the start of the observation by FITS convention (and is what every photometry/occultation/astrometry tool assumes). It should have been 14:04:37 and 14:07:56 respectively.
findings.repro: 1. Imaging, set exposure 30, Snapshot. 2. `grep 'Starting\|Exposure complete' /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/app.log`. 3. Dump DATE-OBS from the written FITS. 4. Repeat with exposure 5 - the error scales with the duration, proving it is end-of-exposure and not clock skew.
findings.evidence: app.log: `14:04:37.849660 Starting 30s exposure` / `14:05:09.054820 Exposure complete`; FITS header `DATE-OBS= '2026-08-01T14:05:09.000Z'` with `EXPTIME = 30.0`. Second pair: `14:07:56.164360 Starting 5s exposure` / `14:08:01.926435 Exposure complete`, `DATE-OBS= '2026-08-01T14:08:01.000Z'`, `EXPTIME = 5.0`.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass `exposureStartedAt` (already in scope at imaging_service.dart) as the FITS captureTimestamp and keep the download time only for captured_images.captured_at. Add DATE-END or EXPEND if the completion time is wanted. Note the sequencer path has the same bug at api/imaging.rs:3383 where capture_timestamp is `chrono::Utc::now()` at header-build time.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced across three different durations in my own log/FITS pairs. 20 s: 'Starting 20s exposure' 15:21:34.986, 'Exposure complete' 15:21:55.903, DATE-OBS='2026-08-01T15:21:55.000Z'. 30 s: start 15:40:36.034, complete 15:41:07.261, DATE-OBS=15:41:07. 3 s: start 15:37:39.198, complete 15:37:42.998, DATE-OBS=15:37:42. In every case DATE-OBS equals the completion instant, so the error scales exactly with EXPTIME (rules out clock skew). Chain confirmed in source: the sim path sets `timestamp: chrono::Utc::now()` when it builds CapturedImageResult after the exposure loop (api/imaging.rs ~line 855); imaging_service.dart:326 does `captureTimestamp = parseUtcTimestamp(capturedImage.timestamp)` while `exposureStartedAt` is already in scope a few lines below; persistence.dart:49 passes it as FitsWriteHeader.captureTimestamp; the writer emits it as DATE-OBS. The footnote about the sequencer is also correct and arguably worse: FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context (api/imaging.rs:3384) hardcodes `capture_timestamp: chrono::Utc::now()` at header-build time, i.e. after download. Severity left at P0: it is silent, systematic, affects every frame from both paths, and invalidates any timing-sensitive science.

findings.title: Framing screen reports the wrong sensor size (1920x1080) for a camera that delivers 4144x2822 - the FOV rectangle is less than half the true width
findings.what_happened: Framing sidebar shows 'Sensor 1920 x 1080', 'FOV 0.78 x 0.44 deg', 'Resolution 1.46 arcsec/px', and the OPTICAL CONFIG overlay repeats '1920 x 1080 px (3.76um)'. The same connected camera in the same app session delivers 4144 x 2822 frames: the Imaging toolbar reads '4144 x 2822', the written FITS has NAXIS1=4144/NAXIS2=2822, and each file is 23,394,240 bytes = 4144*2822*2 + header. At 1.4632 arcsec/px the true FOV is 1.68 x 1.15 deg, so the FOV box drawn over the DSS2 imagery is 2.16x too narrow. A user composing a mosaic or checking whether a target fits would get it badly wrong.
findings.expected: The Framing FOV must be computed from the same sensor geometry the camera actually delivers. Two surfaces of one app must not disagree about one connected camera.
findings.repro: 1. Connect the sim camera. 2. Imaging -> Snapshot -> note '4144 x 2822' in the toolbar and NAXIS1/2 in the FITS. 3. Plan Tonight -> Framing (Send to Framing from any target). 4. Read Sensor/FOV in the sidebar.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-106-addseq.png (OPTICAL CONFIG: 'Simulated Camera / 1920 x 1080 px (3.76um) / FOV 0.78 x 0.44 / Scale 1.46"/px'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-31-done.png (toolbar '4144 x 2822'), FITS header NAXIS1=4144 NAXIS2=2822
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/framing_provider/support.dart:107-109 (pixelsX = status.sensorWidth from backend.getCameraStatus) vs native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sim_frame.rs:41-42 (SIM_W=1920, SIM_H=1080) and native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/devices/simulation.rs:68-69
findings.proposed_fix: Two parts. (a) Finish the unification sim_frame.rs:33-41 claims to have done - the manual-capture path still produces 4144x2822 while status advertises 1920x1080, so 'the frame a caller receives matches the geometry the camera advertised' is currently false. (b) Independently, have the framing FOV cross-check the advertised geometry against the last delivered frame and warn instead of silently drawing a wrong box - on real ASCOM hardware the same split exists between CameraXSize and an active subframe/ROI.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The contradiction reproduces exactly: the Framing sidebar reads 'Sensor 1920 x 1080 / FOV 0.78 x 0.44 / Resolution 1.46 arcsec/px' while the Imaging toolbar reads '4144 x 2822' and every written FITS has NAXIS1=4144 NAXIS2=2822 at 23,394,240 bytes. Third data point I collected: the autofocus path logs '[SEQ] Autofocus point N sample 1/1 completed: 1920x1080 (2073600 pixels)', so two of three paths use 1920x1080 and only manual capture uses 4144x2822 (api/imaging.rs: `full_width = 4144 / bin_x`). sim_frame.rs:32-42 explicitly claims this was unified ('so the frame a caller receives matches the geometry the camera advertised... They previously disagreed three ways') and that claim is false. Two corrections. (a) The title's attribution is backwards: framing_provider/support.dart:100-109 faithfully uses the geometry the camera ADVERTISES (simulation.rs:68-69 sensor_width = SIM_W = 1920); the liar is the manual-capture generator. (b) It is simulator-only — on real ASCOM/INDI hardware the delivered frame matches CameraXSize — so no user with real gear gets a wrong FOV box from this. Reduced to P2 (simulator-fidelity defect, which this project does track as real work).

findings.title: Abort capture does not actually stop the exposure - the camera runs the full duration after "Exposure cancelled"
findings.what_happened: I started a 30 s light at 14:49:49.15, then pressed the toolbar 'Abort capture' X. The native log records 'Exposure cancelled' at 14:50:13.11 (24.0 s in) - and then 'Exposure complete' at 14:50:20.38, i.e. start + 31.2 s, the full exposure. The UI showed 'Stopping...' but the on-image progress ring kept counting to 97% / '1.0s remaining' 4 s after the cancel. The app side handles it correctly (no phantom frame: captured_images stayed at 11 rows and /tmp still had 11 files), but the camera was still integrating and still busy for 7 s after the user was told it had been cancelled. On a 600 s sub that window is ~9.5 minutes during which the app looks Idle and the user is free to slew, change filter or start another capture.
findings.expected: Abort issues a real AbortExposure/StopExposure to the driver, the camera stops within a second, and the UI does not keep counting down a cancelled exposure.
findings.repro: 1. Imaging, exposure 30, Snapshot. 2. After ~20 s press the X (Abort capture) in the preview toolbar. 3. `grep 'Starting\|cancelled\|complete' /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/app.log` and compare timestamps to the requested duration.
findings.evidence: app.log: `14:49:49.146154 Starting 30s exposure` / `14:50:13.111425 Exposure cancelled` / `14:50:20.383265 Exposure complete`; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-99-abort.png (buttons read 'Stopping...' while the ring reads 97% / 1.0s remaining, 4 s after the cancel was logged)
findings.where: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs (cancel path drops the Dart-side await instead of aborting the device exposure); packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:652 ('Abort capture')
findings.proposed_fix: Make the cancel path call the driver's abort and only report 'cancelled' once the device reports not-exposing. Stop the progress ring the moment cancel is issued rather than letting the original timer run out.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The timing reproduces: 'Starting 30s exposure' 15:41:49.208, 'Exposure cancelled' 15:41:57.702 (8.5 s in), 'Exposure complete' 15:42:20.425 = start + 31.2 s. Same shape at 15:26:27/15:26:37/15:26:58. So in the app as driven, cancel is cosmetic and the sim keeps integrating. BUT the stated root cause and the stated consequence are wrong, which materially changes the finding. api_camera_cancel_exposure (api/imaging.rs:1230-1244) branches on the device id: for `sim_` it only sets `camera.status.state = Idle` and logs 'Exposure cancelled' while the exposure future keeps sleeping to completion, then still publishes ExposureComplete{success:true} and stores the frame; for every real device it calls unified_device_ops::mark_camera_exposure_aborted plus DeviceManager::camera_abort_exposure, which reaches the driver's AbortExposure (real_device_ops.rs:1662-1704, device_manager/ops/camera.rs:1178-1248). The claim 'on a 600 s sub that window is ~9.5 minutes during which the camera is still integrating' therefore does not hold for real hardware — this is a simulator no-op, exactly the 'simulators fail in the pass-making direction' class. What IS real on both paths is the UI half: the progress ring keeps counting after cancel, because wait_for_camera_exposure_complete (unified_device_ops.rs:148-203) keeps publishing ExposureProgress until is_complete or the duration+margin deadline. No phantom frame was recorded (captured_images did not gain a row for either cancelled exposure). Reduced to P2.

findings.title: Stretch toggle and stretch-method dropdown do not re-render the frame already on screen - only the NEXT capture picks them up
findings.what_happened: With a captured frame displayed, I toggled Stretch on: the toolbar revealed the STF dropdown but the displayed image was bit-for-bit identical (max pixel diff 0.0 over the whole 980x660 preview). Only after taking a NEW 5 s exposure did the Log stretch apply - preview mean luminance jumped 60.9 -> 153.1 (max pixel diff 192). So the controls do work, they just do not touch the frame you are looking at while you adjust them.
findings.expected: Changing stretch re-renders the current frame instantly. That is the entire point of the control - you adjust it while looking at the sub to judge the result. NINA, ASIAIR and SharpCap all re-render live.
findings.repro: 1. Take a snapshot. 2. Toggle Stretch on; screenshot. 3. Change the method dropdown to Log; screenshot. 4. Diff the preview region of the three screenshots - all zero. 5. Take another snapshot; diff again - large change.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-49-annotationstab.png (stretch off), -50-stretch.png (stretch on), -52-stretch-log.png (Log selected), -53-log-newcapture.png (after a new capture). Numpy diffs over crop (420,300)-(1400,960): off vs on maxdiff 0.0; STF vs Log maxdiff 0.0; Log-before vs Log-after-new-frame mean 60.89 -> 153.09, maxdiff 192.0

findings.proposed_fix: Make the display pipeline watch the stretch settings provider and re-run the tone mapping on the cached frame buffer, so a change repaints without a new exposure.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Half of this does not reproduce, and it is the half the headline rests on. With a captured frame displayed I changed the method from STF to Log and the frame on screen re-rendered immediately, no new capture involved: the same 800x500 preview crop went from mean luminance 59.09 to 148.78 with max pixel diff 113. So the stated root cause ('the stretch parameters are applied during the capture-preview build, not on a settings-change rebuild') is wrong — stretchedImageProvider (auto_stretch_provider.dart:35-83) watches autoStretchSettingsProvider and recomputes live. What IS real is narrower: turning the Stretch toggle OFF does not revert the displayed frame. I toggled it off twice (state verified from the toolbar: knob left, STF dropdown gone) and the preview stayed bit-identical both times (maxdiff 0.0 from the STF render, then maxdiff 1.0 from the Log render). Cause: with enabled=false the provider returns null (auto_stretch_provider.dart:41-43) and image_display.dart:123-128 only re-decodes `if (stretchedData != null)`, so it never falls back to widget.imageData.displayData. That is a P3 fix in one branch, not a P2 'the controls don't touch the frame you are looking at'.

findings.title: Framing sidebar only scrolls when the wheel is over certain sub-regions, and resets to the top on every navigation
findings.what_happened: The Framing sidebar is roughly three viewport-heights tall (Target, Equipment, Frame, Preview FOV, FOV Overlay, Survey Source, Coordinates, Altitude, Mosaic, Guided Framing steps 1-4, Utilities). Mouse-wheel over y=700 did nothing; over y=950/990 it scrolled. Every navigation away and back resets the scroll to the top, so reaching Utilities (Add to Sequence / Auto-build / Save Target / Cache Image) takes 40+ wheel notches from a cold arrival, and clicks land on the wrong control if the layout shifts mid-scroll (twice a click intended for 'Slew to Target' hit the split-button chevron instead).
findings.expected: The whole sidebar is one scrollable, the wheel works anywhere over it, and the scroll offset survives an in-app navigation.
findings.repro: 1. Plan Tonight -> Framing. 2. Wheel over the middle of the sidebar (no movement) then over the bottom (moves). 3. Navigate to Imaging and back - offset resets to top.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-103-utils.png (wheel at y=700, 30 notches, no movement) vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-utils3.png (wheel at y=990 reached Utilities)
findings.proposed_fix: Single outer scrollable with a PageStorageKey so the offset persists; collapse Guided Framing to a compact stepper so Utilities is not below three screens of content.

findings.title: PHD2 cannot be configured during onboarding unless PHD2 is already running
findings.what_happened: The onboarding guider step offers native guiders ('Sim (0)' - there is no simulated guider device) plus a PHD2 block with Host=localhost and Port=4400 prefilled and a Test button. Test correctly reports 'No response on localhost:4400. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?'. But there is no way to SELECT PHD2 as the guider - pressing Next with the prefilled host/port silently discards it, and the review step shows 'Guider - not set -'. So a user setting up indoors before their PHD2 install/first launch cannot record their guider choice at all, and the Guiding screen then greets them with a whole panel of dead-looking controls.
findings.expected: Let the user commit host/port without a successful test (Test stays available as a verification), and record the guider as PHD2 in the profile.
findings.repro: 1. Do not run PHD2. 2. Onboarding -> Guider step -> press Test (honest error) -> press Next. 3. Review step shows 'Guider - not set -'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-09-phd2-test.png (honest test failure), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-08-guider.png (Sim (0) - no simulated guider), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-20-review.png ('Guider - not set -')
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit 'Use PHD2' selection on the onboarding step that persists host/port regardless of Test result. Separately: discovery reports 'Guider: 1 devices' in the log but the onboarding guider list shows 'Sim (0)' - worth reconciling.

findings.title: Default snapshot exposure is 55.0 s
findings.what_happened: On first arrival at the Imaging screen with a fresh profile the Exposure field reads 55.0 sec and the bottom banner reads 'Dur 55 s'. The first thing anyone does on the Imaging screen is take a framing/focus test shot, and 55 s is a minute of waiting before you see anything.
findings.expected: A short default (1-5 s) for the manual Imaging screen, or last-used-value persistence. NINA defaults its manual capture to a short exposure for exactly this reason; long subs belong in the sequencer where the value is set per instruction.
findings.repro: 1. Fresh profile, complete onboarding (camera defaults step asks only for gain/offset, never exposure). 2. Nav -> Imaging. Read the Exposure field.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-27-imaging.png (Exposure 55.0 sec, Dur 55 s) on a profile where no exposure value was ever entered
findings.proposed_fix: Default the Imaging-screen exposure to ~2 s and persist the user's last manual value per profile.

findings.title: Night Narrator ticker produced zero insights across a 65-minute session with 12 frames, an autofocus run and a cooldown
findings.what_happened: NarratorTicker is mounted unconditionally at the top-right of the preview (live_preview_area.dart:629). Over a 65-minute driven session - 12 captures across two filters, a 9-point autofocus that moved best HFR from 2.46 to 2.10, a cooldown from +20 C to -10 C, a filter change, an aborted exposure - the ticker never rendered a single line in any of the ~40 Imaging screenshots. The Transient Alerts bell was likewise empty ('No active alerts'). Either the detectors need a sequencer run to fire, or the feature is invisible on the surface where it is advertised.
findings.expected: At minimum, something like 'Cooling reached -10.0 C' or 'Autofocus improved HFR 2.46 -> 2.10' should surface, since those are exactly the events the narrator is documented to detect.
findings.repro: 1. Imaging screen. 2. Run autofocus, cool the camera, change filter, take frames. 3. Watch the top-right of the preview.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-27-imaging.png through -100-aborted.png (top-right of the preview is empty in every frame), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-101-notifs.png ('No active alerts')
findings.proposed_fix: Confirm whether the narrator requires an active sequencer session; if so, either wire manual-capture events into it or do not mount the ticker on a surface where it can never speak.

verified_correct: Exposure progress, remaining time and the native log agree. For a 30 s exposure the click landed at unix 1785593077.75 and the native log recorded 'Starting 30s exposure' 100 ms later. Sampling the UI at +4.55 s showed 11% / '26.7s remaining' (= 3.3 s elapsed) and at +17.07 s showed 55% / '13.6s remaining' (= 16.4 s elapsed); both are internally self-consistent (percent x 30 s + remaining = 30 s exactly) and within the ~1 s softpipe render lag of wall clock. The exposure completed in 31.2 s for a 30 s request. I attacked this by using two very different durations (30 s and 5 s) and by comparing the ring, the text and the log independently.

Session counters are honest. The Imaging Session card read 'Captured 11 frames / Integration 1m 20s' at a point where captured_images had exactly 11 rows, /tmp had exactly 11 FITS files, and 30 + 10x5 = 80 s = 1m 20s. I tried to break it by mixing snapshots, loop frames and an aborted exposure; the aborted frame correctly did NOT increment any of the three.

Aborting a capture does not fabricate a frame. After pressing Abort on a 30 s exposure, captured_images stayed at 11 rows, /tmp stayed at 11 files, and the preview reverted to the previous good frame. (The underlying device abort is still broken - reported separately - but the app-level bookkeeping is truthful.)

PHD2 Connect gives a specific, actionable error with no PHD2 installed: 'PHD2 connection failed: PHD2 is not running and could not be launched automatically. Install PHD2 or set Settings -> PHD2 Guiding -> PHD2 executable path.' plus a 'PHD2 not running - searching for installed PHD2...' notification. The onboarding Test button is equally specific. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-74-connectphd2.png. This is the one place in the guiding area that does the right thing, and it is the model the dead Start/Loop/Auto Select buttons should follow.

Autofocus runs a real 9-point sweep and produces a real V curve. 4/9 -> 9/9 progress, focuser position tracked the sweep (25050 -> 25250 -> settled at 25075, exactly SIM_TRUE_FOCUS), HFR improved 3.21 -> 2.10, and the fitted minimum matched the simulator's true focus. Manual focus nudge moved 25000 -> 25050 with step size 50 as configured. Evidence imaging-guiding-38/39/40 and crop-focus1/crop-focus2/crop-af3.png. I tried to break it by nudging the focuser off-centre first so the sweep was asymmetric; it still found the right minimum.

Camera cooling works and reports truthfully: target -10 C, Cool Down took the sensor 20.0 -> -10.0 C in ~30 s with cooler power ramping to 100% then settling to 63%, and the -10.0 C value propagated to the bottom status bar, the bottom-banner temp segment and CCD-TEMP in later FITS headers. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-cooling2.png.

Guiding no-data readouts are mostly honest: 'PHD2 Disconnected' in the header, 'Stopped' chip, 'Connect a guider to acquire a guide star' in the Guide Star card, RA/Dec/Tot '---' on the guide graph, Star Statistics SNR '---' / Star Mass '---' / Frame Count 0, and Calibration 'Not Calibrated'. Evidence imaging-guiding-70 and -77. The only dishonest numbers are the two Peak fields (reported separately).

Custom annotation drawing works end to end: selecting the circle tool, dragging on the image, entering a label in the 'Circle Label' dialog and pressing Add produced a correctly-placed dashed circle with the label 'TestCircle' rendered beneath it, and it persisted across a subsequent capture. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-circle.png and imaging-guiding-100-aborted.png (still present).

The Science HUD's frame count is truthful: 'Science up to date - 11 frames processed' matched exactly 11 rows in science_frame_quality_metrics. I checked this specifically because a fabricated 'processed' count would be the highest-value lie on that panel.

The Framing wizard's plate-solver step is honest and specific: step 3 shows 'Ready' but carries an explicit 'Plate solver not configured - The framing wizard solves the latest camera exposure to measure how far the mount is from your target. Set up ASTAP (or Astrometry.net) to enable this step.' with a working 'Set up plate solver' action. Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-utils2.png.

Onboarding blocks Next when no capture folder is chosen, and validates the chosen folder ('Folder is writable'). I specifically tried to get past that step with an empty folder field and it refused. Evidence imaging-guiding-14-nofolder-next.png and -18-folderdone.png.

Optical-train math is correct: 206.265 x 3.76 / 530 = 1.4632 arcsec/px and the app displayed 1.46 arcsec/px in onboarding, on the Framing sidebar and on the OPTICAL CONFIG card. The Framing FOV numbers are also arithmetically consistent with the (wrong) 1920x1080 sensor it believes in - 1920 x 1.4632 = 0.779 deg - so the FOV bug is purely the sensor input, not the geometry.

Filter-wheel indexing is consistent between UI and API: the Equipment card displays 1-based positions (R = #2) while the API call is 0-based (clicking Ha logged 'api_filterwheel_set_position ... position=4' for the 5th filter). The wheel physically moved and the chip highlight followed. The failure is purely that the selection never reaches the capture metadata.
coverage_note: Drove the real release bundle on display :87 with profile `imaging-guiding` for ~75 minutes: full onboarding with the Sim backend (530 mm f/5.0, 3.76 um, gain 100/offset 50, 7-filter wheel), Connect All (5 devices; guider deliberately left disconnected to exercise the no-PHD2 path), 12 real simulated exposures, a 9-point autofocus, a cooldown to -10 C, a Loop run, an abort, a full pass over all 8 right-hand Imaging tabs, the Guiding screen, and the Framing screen with a real target (M92) and live DSS2 HiPS imagery. 115 screenshots under /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-*.png. Findings were cross-checked against three independent sources rather than the UI alone: the scratch SQLite DB at /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/data/skotiq.db, the raw FITS headers written to /tmp, and the native log at /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/app.log. Pixel-level claims (stretch no-op, zoom scale) were measured numerically with numpy, not eyeballed. IMPORTANT HARNESS LIMITATION: `drive_linux.py tree` never worked for this instance - every invocation returned 'no Skotiq accessibility root found for our pid', so I could not read [ON]/[off]/[DISABLED] states and had to infer enablement from rendering plus click outcome plus source. That is why the Guiding-controls finding is framed as 'disabled state is visually indistinguishable' (source proves they are gated on isConnected) rather than 'enabled control does nothing'. Two units are phone-only and unreachable on a fixed 1600x900 desktop window (fullscreen_image_viewer, guiding/mobile_sections); two more need capability I do not have in this environment (centering_dialog needs a plate solver, meridian_flip_countdown_banner needs a tracking mount near the meridian); one (focus_model_panel) is unreachable by construction and is itself reported as a defect. I did NOT rebuild anything. The five most serious items - filter attribution lost on every frame, DATE-OBS off by one exposure length, Add-to-Sequence adding nothing, Loop filling the disk, and the 2.16x-wrong Framing FOV - are each reproducible in under two minutes with the steps above.
